title: Ladder Inspection Checklist and OSHA Checklist (29 CFR 1926.1053)
subtitle: For periodic competent-person inspections and after any occurrence that may have damaged or disturbed a ladder.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
If a ladder has a structural defect, mark it as defective or tag it “Do Not Use” and keep it out of service until it is repaired (1926.1053(b)(16) and (b)(17)).
Record any other failed set-up or use item and correct it before the ladder is used.

sections.title: Condition of portable ladders
items: A competent person has checked the ladder for visible defects as part of periodic inspections and after any event that might have affected it
Rungs, cleats and steps parallel, level and uniformly spaced with the ladder in position for use
No broken or split rails and no corroded components
Any ladder with a structural defect is marked as defective or tagged “Do Not Use” and kept out of service until repaired
Rungs and steps corrugated, knurled, dimpled, skid-resistant coated or otherwise treated
No surface that could puncture or cut a worker or snag clothing
No opaque paint or covering; labels only on one face of a side rail
Rungs, steps and rails clean of oil, grease and other slippery material
Repaired ladders restored to their original design criteria before reuse

sections.title: Stepladders
items: Metal spreader or locking device present and engaged, holding front and back sections open
Nobody standing on the top or top step
Rear bracing not climbed unless the ladder has steps on both front and rear sections

sections.title: Set-up and placement
items: Side rails reach 3 feet or more above the upper landing, or the top is secured to a rigid non-deflecting support with a grabrail or other grasping device
Horizontal distance from top support to foot about a quarter of the ladder's working length (non-self-supporting ladders)
Horizontal distance from top support to foot is one-eighth of the working length (wood job-made ladders with spliced side rails)
Both rails bearing equally at the top, unless a single support attachment is fitted
Stable, level surface, or ladder secured against accidental displacement
Ladder secured or fitted with slip-resistant feet, and still placed, lashed or held with care
In passageways, doorways or driveways, ladder secured or traffic barricaded away
No materials or debris around the top and bottom of the ladder
Ladders not tied or fastened together for length unless designed for it
Separate ladders serving one elevated area offset with a platform or landing between them

sections.title: Use and climbing
items: Ladder not loaded beyond its maximum intended load or the manufacturer's rated capacity
Ladder used only for the purpose it was designed for
Nonconductive siderails where the worker or ladder could contact exposed energized electrical equipment
Ladder not moved, shifted or extended with anyone on it
Climbers face the ladder going up and down
Climbers hold on with one hand or more while moving
Nothing carried that could unbalance the climber

sections.title: Fixed ladders
items: Ladder with structural defects tagged, marked or blocked and out of service until repaired
Cage, well, ladder safety device or self-retracting lifeline where the top is more than 24 feet above lower levels

Ladder safety device; or self-retracting lifelines with rest platforms no more than 150 feet apart; or cage or well with offset sections of 50 feet or less and landing platforms at intervals of 50 feet or less
7 inches or more to any obstruction behind the ladder (4 1/2 inches for elevator pit ladders)
30 inches or more from rung centerline to obstructions, unless reduced under (a)(15) with a deflection device
Side rails of through or side-step ladders extend 42 inches above the access level or landing platform
Side clearance without cage or well
15 inches or more clear on each side of the ladder centerline to the nearest permanent object
Pitch no greater than 90 degrees from horizontal, measured to the back side of the ladder

references: 29 CFR 1926.1053: Ladders (Part 1926, Subpart X: Stairways and Ladders)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, text as of 2026-11-09
